papers.title: Polygraphic resolutions for operated algebras
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the structure of operated polygraphs as a categorical model for rewriting in operated algebras, generalizing Gr\"obner--Shirshov bases with non-monomial termination orders. We show how to construct polygraphic resolutions of free operated algebras from confluent and terminating presentations. We provide a combinatorial description of critical branchings of operated polygraphs using the structure of polyautomata introduced in this paper. Polyautomata are linear polygraphs equipped with an operator structure formalized by a pushdown automaton. Finally, we apply our constructions to several families of operated algebras, including Rota--Baxter algebras, differential algebras, and differential Rota--Baxter algebras.

papers.title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
papers.abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.

papers.title: Quasi-projective dimensions of complexes over rings
papers.abstract: Quasi-projective dimension of modules over associative rings is generalized in this paper to the one of complexes of modules. Basic properties of this dimension are established, including a comparison result with projective dimension and a derived Auslander-Buchsbaum formula for complexes of finite quasi-projective dimension. Several sufficient conditions are provided for a commutative noetherian local ring to be a complete intersection under the assumption that each finitely generated module has finite quasi-projective dimension. This provides some positive answers to an open question on quasi-projective dimension proposed by Gheibi-Jorgensen-Takahashi. Moreover, the behavior of quasi-projective dimension under taking the quotient of a commutative ring modulo a regular sequence is investigated, and some partial results toward the change-of-rings question on quasi-projective dimension are given.

papers.title: The ozone group of $U_q^+(B_2)$
papers.abstract: We determine the ozone group of \(U_q^{+}(B_2)\). More precisely, if \(\ell=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)\) when \(q\) is a root of unity, we obtain $$ \operatorname{Oz}(U_q^{+}(B_2)) \cong \begin{cases} \mu_2 , & \text{if \(q\) is not a root of unity},\\[2mm] \mu_{\gcd(\ell,2)}, & \text{if \(q\) is a primitive \(m\)-th root of unity, \(m\geq5\).} \end{cases} $$ We also study several homological properties of \(U_q^{+}(B_2)\), showing that it is Artin--Schelter regular of global dimension \(4\), Auslander-regular, Cohen--Macaulay, strongly Noetherian, and skew Calabi--Yau. Using two different iterated Ore presentations, we show that its Nakayama automorphism is trivial for every $q \in \K^*$, so $U_q^{+}(B_2)$ is Calabi--Yau of dimension $4$; for $q$ not a root of unity this also follows from work of Goodearl and Yakimov. When $q$ is a primitive $m$-th root of unity with $m\geq5$, we deduce that the center is Gorenstein, we check directly that the ozone group acts with trivial homological determinant, and we describe the nonzero normal elements in terms of the ozone group.

papers.title: Two Short Proofs of the $A^A$ Theorem
papers.abstract: In 1984, D.~Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ implies $A\cong B$ for finite, nonempty ordered sets $A$ and~$B$. J.\,D. Farley and the author proved that it does. In this paper, we give two short proofs using all intervals of maximum height and the elements with exactly one lower cover. The first proof averages over these intervals; the second takes their disjoint sum and constructs three invariants. Both avoid the auxiliary ordering, direct factorization, and canonical coordinates of the earlier proof.

papers.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.

papers.title: A Krause-type recollement for Q-shaped derived categories
papers.abstract: Let k be a commutative noetherian hereditary ring and let Q be a small, Hom-finite, locally bounded k-linear category admitting a Serre functor and satisfying the strong retraction property, with nilpotent pseudo-radical. For every k-algebra A, we construct a recollement of the Q-shaped homo?topy category KQ(A Inj) of objectwise injective Q-shaped modules by its full subcategory Kac Q (A Inj) of exact objects and the Q-shaped derived category DQ(A). The construction uses complete hereditary cotorsion pairs and does not require A to be noetherian. If A is left noetherian, both KQ(A Inj) and Kac Q (A Inj) are compactly generated by special preenvelopes of finitely generat?ed stalk modules. We identify (Kac Q (A Inj))c with the idempotent completion of (KQ(A Inj))c/LI ((DQ(A))c ), where LI is the fully faithful left adjoint of the localization. This paper builds on and generalizes works of Krause and Liu

papers.title: Star-Ordered Rotor Loops in Clifford Algebras
papers.abstract: We consider, in a real Clifford algebra, a family of unit bivectors $B_i = C S_i$ formed from $k+1$ pairwise anticommuting generators $C, S_1, \ldots, S_k$ with square $-1$; we call this a \emph{star family} with \emph{central generator} $C$ and \emph{leaf generators} $S_i$. For the associated rotors $U_i(\theta_i) = \cos\frac{\theta_i}{2} + B_i \sin\frac{\theta_i}{2}$ we study two objects: the ordered chain $P_k = U_1 \cdots U_k$ and the \emph{star-ordered rotor loop} $\Theta_k = P_k \, Q_k$ with the \emph{same-order reversion product} $Q_k = \widetilde U_1 \cdots \widetilde U_k$, as opposed to the trivially reversed order, for which $U_1 \cdots U_k \widetilde U_k \cdots \widetilde U_1 = 1$. The scalar part of $\Theta_k$ measures the \emph{order defect} of the family. We prove two theorems. First, the scalar part of the chain factorises, $\langle P_k \rangle_0 = \prod_{i=1}^k \cos\frac{\theta_i}{2}$; this requires the star structure, and we give a counterexample. Second, we derive a closed expression for $\langle \Theta_k \rangle_0$, valid for every $k$, whose coefficients obey a \emph{period-four sign law} $\eta(m) = (-1)^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor}$ and which admits the compact form $\langle \Theta_k \rangle_0 = \operatorname{Re}\!\big[(1-\mathrm{i}) \prod_i (\cos^2\frac{\theta_i}{2} + \mathrm{i}\sin^2\frac{\theta_i}{2})\big]$, holding for every pairwise anticommuting unit family without further hypothesis. From the compact form we obtain a polar form, a complete zero criterion, a lacunary coefficient rule, and a proof of non-separability for $k \geq 2$. Two supplementary theorems extend the result to arbitrary permutations of the index order and to families with mixed squares $B_i^2 \in \{-1, +1\}$. All proofs use only anticommutation, reversion and the symmetry of the scalar form; no physical interpretation is assumed or claimed.

papers.title: A proof of the interlacing conjecture for the singular values of Sylvester-Kac matrices
papers.abstract: Boros and R\'ozsa (Linear Algebra Appl. 421 (2007) 407--416) reduced the singular value problem for the odd-order Sylvester--Kac matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{(2m+1)\times(2m+1)}$ to those for $Q^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{(m+1)\times m}$ and $S^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m+1)}$ via a permutation similarity transformation. They noted that $(Q^{(m)})^{T}Q^{(m)}-S^{(m)}(S^{(m)})^{T}$ is positive definite, and also conjectured that $\sigma_i(S^{(m)})\ge\sigma_{i+1}(Q^{(m)})$ for $1\le i\le m-1$ and $m\ge2$. In this paper, we prove that these inequalities are strict and establish the strict interlacing relation \begin{equation*} \sigma_1(Q^{(m)})>\sigma_1(S^{(m)})> \cdots>\sigma_m(Q^{(m)})> \sigma_m(S^{(m)})>0 \end{equation*} for all $m\ge1$. Here, $\sigma_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th largest singular value of a matrix.

papers.title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
papers.abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_\delta$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_\delta$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

papers.title: Approximation of graded bialgebras
papers.abstract: Motivated by an equivalence of categories established by Kapranov and Schechtman, we introduce, for each non-negative integer d, the category of connected bialgebras modulo d+1. We show that these categories fit into an inverse system of categories whose inverse limit category is equivalent to the category of connected bialgebras. In addition, we extend the notion of approximation of connected bialgebras to those that are not necessarily generated in degree 1 and show that, for connected bialgebras in the category of Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a Hopf algebra, approximation is compatible with cocycle twisting.

papers.title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $\rho\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $\rho^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+\rho+\rho^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langle\rho\rangle$ when $\rho$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.

papers.title: Differential equations as difference-differential equations
papers.abstract: We analyze the behavior of systems of algebraic differential equations when considered as systems of difference-differential equations, with special emphasis on systems which define minimal sets relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCF}$ of differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ distinguished commuting derivations. We show that if $p$ is a minimal type relative to $\operatorname{DCF}$ defined by a system of algebraic partial differential equations and inequations and the forking geometry on $p$ is trivial (also called ``disintegrated''), then $p$ remains minimal when regarded as a partial type relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCFA}$ of difference-differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ commuting derivations in the sense that every completion has $\operatorname{SU}$-rank one. We illustrate this theorem by describing in detail the possible difference-differential equations consistent with differential equations of the form $y' = y^3 + a_2 y^2 + a_1 y + a_0$ where $a_0$, $a_1$, and $a_2$ are differential constants.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
papers.abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

papers.title: Low-rank perturbation of symplectic matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper the generic behavior of the Jordan structure of symplectic matrices under low-rank structure-preserving transformations is considered. So far, only the case of rank-one perturbations was covered in the literature, and this result is now extended to the case of arbitrary rank $k$. As a key step toward the main result, it is shown that all symplectic matrices that differ from the identity by rank $k$ can be represented as a product of $k$ symplectic reflectors unless they are similar to a diagonalizable matrix having only the eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

papers.title: Characterizations in terms of Generalized Inverses
papers.abstract: Using simply outer inverse and their differences, we characterize many known classes of rings including von Neumann regular, unit-regular, exchange, clean, and strongly clean rings.

papers.title: Zhang twists for semigroups and groupoids, with applications to Steinberg algebras
papers.abstract: Zhang twists provide a powerful mechanism for deforming graded algebras, while preserving their graded module categories. We extend this theory by introducing Zhang twists for graded semigroups and graded ample groupoids. We show that the twisting construction preserves a broad class of semigroup structures, and that two graded monoids are twists of each other if and only if their categories of graded sets are pointedly equivalent. We show that Zhang twists are compatible with noncommutative Stone duality: twists on graded-Boolean inverse semigroups are in correspondence with those on the associated graded ample groupoids. Moreover, in the setting of Steinberg algebras we prove that twisting the groupoid gives the same result as twisting the corresponding algebra. These results provide a unified framework linking graded semigroups, inverse semigroup duality, ample groupoids, and graded algebras, while extending the scope of Zhang twists to settings arising from symbolic dynamics, graph algebras, and Steinberg algebras.

papers.title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

papers.title: Ideals in Enveloping Algebras of Loop Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra, and consider the loop algebra $L\mathfrak g = \mathfrak g[s, s^{-1}]$ and the affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak g}$, which is an extension of $L\mathfrak g$ by a central element $c$. It is known that the rings $\operatorname{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c-\lambda)$ are simple for any nonzero scalar $\lambda$. On the other hand, the universal enveloping algebra $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g) \cong \mathrm{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c)$ has many two-sided ideals, and in this paper we investigate their structure. We show that the two-sided structure of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ is both intricate and well-behaved. Specifically, $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ does not satisfy the ascending chain condition on two-sided ideals, but the two-sided ideals still have a nice structure: there is a canonical nested collection of ideals $I_n$, parameterised by positive integers, so that any nonzero two-sided ideal of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ contains all $I_n$ for $n \gg 0$. The ideals $I_n$ can be thought of as universal annihilators of natural classes of finite-dimensional representations of $L\mathfrak g$. We also study the Poisson structure of the symmetric algebra $\mathrm{S}(L\mathfrak g)$ and give applications to the representation theory of $L\mathfrak g$.

papers.title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.

papers.title: Evolution algebras: a survey of results and a list of open problems
papers.abstract: Evolution algebras, introduced by J. P. Tian as an algebraic model of non- Mendelian inheritance, are commutative algebras with a basis whose distinct elements multiply to zero. The first part of the paper surveys the theory: low-dimensional classifica- tions, structure theory, nilpotency, automorphisms and derivations, directed graphs and random walks, infinite-dimensional and dynamical aspects, and embedding theorems. The second part is a unified list of fifty open questions and eleven new conjectures, each accompanied by the available evidence; two of the conjectures and one of the questions are settled here. We also prove several new observations, most of them formally verified in the proof assistant Lean (see Section 2.1.11): every finite group is the automorphism group of a simple evolution algebra over every field, and | Aut(A)|/ dim A takes every positive ratio- nal value on simple evolution algebras over every field; infinitude of the automorphism group of nilpotent algebras, the possible numbers of idempotents of real perfect evolution algebras, a Galois-theoretic criterion for the existence of idempotents in dimension two, the average number of idempotents over finite fields, and a perfect evolution algebra whose automorphism group is a non-split extension.

papers.title: On partial representations of pointed Hopf algebras
papers.abstract: The theory of partial representations first appeared in the context of groups to deal with restrictions of representations to non-invariant subspaces. Partial representations of a group $G$ correspond to representations of a groupoid algebra constructed out of $G$. The notion of a partial representation can be extended to the context of Hopf algebras. For a Hopf algebra $H$, its partial representations correspond to representations of a Hopf algebroid $H_{par}$, also constructed out of data coming from $H$. In this work, we describe the structure of the algebra $H_{par}$ for $H$ being a pointed Hopf algebra with a finite group of grouplikes $G(H)$. This algebra can be explicitly written as a direct sum, reflecting the groupoid algebra associated to the group $G(H)$. Explicit examples of rank one Hopf algebras are done in the nilpotent and the non-nilpotent cases.

papers.title: Nonassociative algebras of anti-biderivation-type
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to study the class of Jacobi-Jordan-admissible algebras whose product is an anti-biderivation of the related Jacobi-Jordan algebra; we call them $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras. We give characterizations of $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras and show that this class includes Jacobi-Jordan algebras, symmetric anti-Leibniz algebras and anti-${\rm LR}$-algebras. The derived algebra of an anti-${\rm LR}$-algebra is associative and commutative, and all identities of its commutator algebra follow from the metabelian identity and one identity of degree $4$. We also study $\mathcal A$flexible ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras and prove that a complex finite-dimensional Jacobi-Jordan algebra admits a non-trivial post-Jacobi-Jordan structure if and only if its dimension is at least $3$. Finally, we give the algebraic classification of complex $3$-dimensional $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras and show that complex finite-dimensional simple ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras are anticommutative, while perfect ones need not be; the minimal dimension of perfect non-anticommutative ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras is $4$.

papers.title: Fusion rules from the Norton inequality
papers.abstract: The Norton inequality is one of the fundamental axioms in the theory of Majorana and axial algebras, yet its precise structural consequences have remained only partially understood. In this paper, we show that the Norton inequality alone forces the $0$- and $1$-eigenspace fusion rules for arbitrary idempotents in a commutative real algebra $A$ equipped with a Frobenius form. More precisely, if the Frobenius form is nondegenerate (as in Majorana algebras), we prove that the eigenspaces $A_0(e)$ and $A_1(e)$ of an arbitrary idempotent $e \in A$ are subalgebras and annihilate one another: \[ A_0(e)A_1(e)=\{0\}, \] while in the degenerate case the corresponding inclusions hold modulo the radical of the Frobenius form. This answers a question of T. M. Mudziiri Shumba and S. Shpectorov concerning the closure of the $0$-eigenspace $A_0(e)$.

papers.title: Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems II
papers.abstract: The paper "Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems II" continues the line of "Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems" from the perspective of almost classical localizations of algebras and the conclusions of K.~I.~Beidar's doctoral dissertation. This allows one to apply the orthogonal completion method to describe non-degenerate orthogonally complete algebras bases on known classifications of strongly prime algebras.

papers.title: The $\phi$-conjugation of quaternionic matrices and generalized Autonne-Takagi factorization
papers.abstract: Let $\phi$ be a quaternion of modulus $1$. In this article, we study some topics related to $\phi$-conjugation for quaternionic matrices, including $\phi$-Hermitian matrices, $\phi$-conjugate normal matrices, unitary $\phi$-congruence and $\phi$-HSH decomposition (decomposition of a $\phi$-Hermitian matrix and a skew $\phi$-Hermitian matrix). In particular, we generalize the Autonne-Takagi factorization of quaternion $\phi$-Hermitian matrices for all unit quaternion $\phi$. This gives an affirmative answer to a problem proposed by R. Horn and F. Zhang in the paper ``A generalization of the complex Autonne-Takagi factorization to quaternion matrices, Linear Multilinear A. 60: 1239--1244, 2012''.

papers.title: Algebraic derivations and radicals of automorphism groups of algebras
papers.abstract: The paper "Algebraic derivations and radicals of automorphism groups of algebras" continues both the well-known line of description of algebraic derivations of semiprime associative algebras in terms of inner derivations of their symmetric Martindale rings of quotients, and results on the coincidence of the prime and weakly solvable radicals of subgroups of multiplicative groups of PI-rings using the example of automorphism groups of algebras associated with their algebraic derivations.
